title: A2UIVerse Shell Catalog
description: The shell's paint vocabulary: the A2UI basic catalog plus the composition primitives Slot and Attribution.

text.description: The text content to display. While simple Markdown formatting is supported (i.e. without HTML, images, or links), utilizing dedicated UI components is generally preferred for a richer and more structured presentation.

variant.description: A hint for the base text style.

url.description: The URL of the image to display.

fit.description: Specifies how the image should be resized to fit its container. This corresponds to the CSS 'object-fit' property.

variant.description: A hint for the image size and style.

name.description: The name of the icon to display.

url.description: The URL of the video to display.

posterUrl.description: The URL of the poster image to display before the video plays.

url.description: The URL of the audio to be played.

description.description: A description of the audio, such as a title or summary.

Row.description: A layout component that arranges its children horizontally. To create a grid layout, nest Columns within this Row.

children.description: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list. Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID.

justify.description: Defines the arrangement of children along the main axis (horizontally). Use 'spaceBetween' to push items to the edges, or 'start'/'end'/'center' to pack them together.

align.description: Defines the alignment of children along the cross axis (vertically). This is similar to the CSS 'align-items' property, but uses camelCase values (e.g., 'start').

Column.description: A layout component that arranges its children vertically. To create a grid layout, nest Rows within this Column.

children.description: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list. Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID.

justify.description: Defines the arrangement of children along the main axis (vertically). Use 'spaceBetween' to push items to the edges (e.g. header at top, footer at bottom), or 'start'/'end'/'center' to pack them together.

align.description: Defines the alignment of children along the cross axis (horizontally). This is similar to the CSS 'align-items' property.

children.description: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list.

direction.description: The direction in which the list items are laid out.

align.description: Defines the alignment of children along the cross axis.

child.description: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID.

tabs.description: An array of objects, where each object defines a tab with a title and a child component.

child.description: The ID of the child component.

trigger.description: The ID of the component that opens the modal when interacted with (e.g., a button).

content.description: The ID of the component to be displayed inside the modal.

child.description: The ID of the child component. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button. Only use an 'Icon' if the requirements explicitly ask for an icon-only button.

variant.description: A hint for the button style. If omitted, a default button style is used. 'primary' indicates this is the main call-to-action button. 'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link.

label.description: The text label for the input field.

value.description: The value of the text field.

placeholder.description: The placeholder text for the input field.

variant.description: The type of input field to display.

label.description: The text to display next to the checkbox.

value.description: The current state of the checkbox (true for checked, false for unchecked).

ChoicePicker.description: A component that allows selecting one or more options from a list.

label.description: The label for the group of options.

variant.description: A hint for how the choice picker should be displayed and behave.

options.description: The list of available options to choose from.

label.description: The text to display for this option.

value.description: The stable value associated with this option.
The list of currently selected values. This should be bound to a string array in the data model.

displayStyle.description: The display style of the component.

filterable.description: If true, displays a search input to filter the options.

min.description: The minimum value of the slider.

max.description: The maximum value of the slider.

value.description: The current value of the slider.

steps.description: The number of discrete divisions in the slider range. If specified, the slider will snap to discrete values.

value.description: The selected date and/or time value in ISO 8601 format. If not yet set, initialize with an empty string.

enableDate.description: If true, allows the user to select a date.

enableTime.description: If true, allows the user to select a time.

min.description: The minimum allowed date/time in ISO 8601 format.

max.description: The maximum allowed date/time in ISO 8601 format.

label.description: The text label for the input field.

Slot.description: A named region of a composed screen whose content is mounted by the client. Paint one per planned fragment; later repaints may change its state but never its position. While no content has arrived it renders a pending placeholder. A slot whose content is the shell's own — the merged view — is declared `content: "shell"`: it keeps its reserved position but is painted like the shell's own UI, with no tile: while pending it is reserved as the merged view's label, its planned column headers and a few skeleton rows, and the view takes its own height when it lands. A source that fails shows the failure tile in its region: the failure said in the shell's words, Retry, and the vendor's own words beneath. A source that needs sign-in shows the authority tile in its region. A source whose app needs an update to show its answer shows the update tile in its region, kept while its answer is sent again. An app with two or more accounts, for a command that named none, shows the account choice in its region. A collapsed merge leaves its slot as one line saying why: the Synthesizer's reason when it declined, the shell's own words otherwise.

source.description: The dispatched source whose content fills the region: a source id — the app and the account it paints under, `<appId>.<n>`, the bare app id for an app needing no sign-in — or `shell` for the merged view. The slot's identity within the layout; unique per surface. A slot holds exactly one of `source`, `gap`, `chooseAccount` or `addAccount`.

gap.description: A capability no installed app serves, in words — the words this plan searched the Store for. The region is the offer, drawn as fixed shell UI: the apps the plan offered from the Store, each with Install, or one line when there is nothing to offer. Once an offered app is installed there, the region becomes that app's. A slot holds exactly one of `source`, `gap`, `chooseAccount` or `addAccount`.

chooseAccount.description: An app id: the app has two or more accounts and the command for it named none. The region is drawn as a fixed tile asking which account to use, one press per account; the press sends the request planned for the app to that account, and its answer fills this region. A slot holds exactly one of `source`, `gap`, `chooseAccount` or `addAccount`.

addAccount.description: An app id: the utterance asked to add an account to the app. The region is drawn as a fixed tile — the accounts already added, what a new account lets the app do, and the press opening the app's sign-in for a new account. Write nothing else for it. A slot holds exactly one of `source`, `gap`, `chooseAccount` or `addAccount`.

accounts.description: With `chooseAccount` or `addAccount` only: the app's accounts — those the choice offers, or those already added — each its source id and its label. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

state.description: The region’s lifecycle state, painted by the runtime and never written by an author. `pending` shows a placeholder until content arrives; `failed` shows the failure tile; `collapsed` removes the region from view without moving its neighbours; `authority` shows the authority tile; `update` shows the update tile.

label.description: Human-readable name for the awaited content, shown while pending or failed.

noun.description: Fragment content only: what the source was asked for, as the merged view's join calls it — "CircleCI runs". Written beside `label` at plan time; the failure tile's line is composed from the two.

failure.description: Fragment content only: why the source failed. Painted by the runtime with `state: "failed"` and never written by an author.

cause.description: `vendor`: the vendor ended its task failed; `unreachable`: the connection or stream broke, nothing said; `timeout`: no answer within the time allowed; `invalid`: the paint arrived and could not be rendered; `catalog`: the agent painted in a catalog the app is not entitled to; `uninstalled`: the app is no longer installed; `load`: the client could not load the catalog the paint is in; `credential`: the agent painted a credential field and did not repair it — no Retry; `interface`: the app's card lists no interface the platform speaks, so the agent was not called; `unconfirmed`: the app's live card is signed and did not pass the check, so the agent was not called.

message.description: The vendor's own words, only with `cause: "vendor"` and only when the vendor gave any.

catalogId.description: The catalog the agent painted in, only with `cause: "catalog"` or `cause: "load"`.

continueUrl.description: Only with `cause: "credential"`, when the app has one: its own page, from its card's provider URL or documentation URL, https only, localhost exempt.

authority.description: Fragment content only: the slot's sign-in. Painted by the runtime with `state: "authority"` and never written by an author.

cause.description: `signIn`: no usable account for this app; `connect`: the same, for an app connected with a pasted key or token; `more`: an account is held and the app asks it for more access; `again`: the account's sign-in ran out and the silent refresh failed; `unsupported`: the app asks for a kind of sign-in A2UIVerse cannot do.

quiet.description: With `cause: "signIn"`, `"connect"` or `"more"` only: the one-line form, after the full tile for this app was shown once this session.

scopes.description: With `cause: "signIn"`, `"connect"` or `"more"`, required there: what the app will be able to do, in the words of its card — none for a key or a token.

update.description: Fragment content only: the slot's update tile — the app cannot show its answer in what it is installed with, or now asks for access it was not installed with. Painted by the runtime with `state: "update"`, and kept with `state: "pending"` while its answer is sent again; never written by an author.

state.description: The app's update state, which the tile's line follows: `update-required`, `major-update` and `card-update` — the Store has a version the app can show its answer in, with Update; `ahead-of-store`, `up-to-date` and `newer-build` — the Store is waiting on the publisher; `unknown` — the Store could not be reached, with Retry; `not-published` — the Store has no update for it.

publishedVersion.description: The Store's version of the app, whenever the Store has its entry.

newScopes.description: With `update-required`, `major-update` or `card-update`, required there: what the Store's version newly asks, by scheme and scope keys; any at all and its Update asks for consent first.

publisher.description: The app's publisher, whenever the Store has its entry.

scopes.description: With `addAccount` only: what a new account lets the app do, in the words of the app's card. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

content.description: Whose content fills the region. `fragment` is an agent's surface, mounted inside its boundary with the attribution painted beside the slot; `shell` is the shell's own content, rendered in place with no boundary and no attribution, reserved under its planned columns while pending.

columns.description: Shell content only: the merged view's planned column headers, in order, drawn over the skeleton rows while pending.

columnSources.description: Shell content only: one entry per planned column, the source id the column belongs to — the source whose values it shows — or null for a column of no single source. The same length as `columns`. A column whose source has not answered is drawn reserved: its heading says so and its cells hold a bar until the source arrives.

join.description: Shell content only: the entity the merged view joins, as each source calls it — `home`, the source whose instances are the rows, and `nouns`, a plural noun per source id. Not drawn by the slot; the host reads it to say what is being joined.

home.description: The source whose entries are the rows, by id; null when the join is a union, the rows every entry any source lists, entries of the same thing merged into one row.

entity.description: When `home` is null: the thing the union joins, in a plural noun.

declined.description: Shell content only: the reason the merge was declined, in the Synthesizer's words. Painted by the runtime with `state: "collapsed"` and never written by an author; drawn as one line where the merged view's label would have sat.

collapse.description: Shell content only: why the merge collapsed when it was not declined. Painted by the runtime with `state: "collapsed"` and never written by an author; drawn as one line in the shell's words where the merged view's label would have sat.

cause.description: `home`: the home source failed, so nothing can be joined; `few`: fewer than two sources answered; `unmade`: the merged view couldn't be made.

home.description: With `cause: "home"` only: the home source's entries as the join calls them — "Linear issues".

answered.description: With `cause: "few"` only: the display names of the sources that answered, none or one.

failed.description: With `cause: "few"` only: the sources dispatched that did not arrive, by id.

merged.description: Shell content only: the source ids the landed merged view was built over. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

late.description: Shell content only: the source ids that arrived after the merge — landed, declined or not made — and wait for the reader to include them. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

working.description: Shell content only: a call the reader's press caused is running. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

sources.description: The source ids the call folds in; none when it makes the view afresh or updates it.

callFailed.description: Shell content only: the last call the reader's press caused failed and the landed view was kept. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

kind.description: `include`: the sources it folded in stay out of the view; `update`: the view was left as it was.

sources.description: With `kind: "include"`: the source ids it left out; none otherwise.

retrying.description: Shell content only, on a collapsed merge: the retried source ids whose arrival brings the merge back. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

offer.description: With `gap` only: the offer, from the marketplace's entries. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

apps.description: Every app the plan offered, in its order: its app id, its name, its publisher and its short description.

none.description: With no app offered, required there: why. `nothing`: nothing in the Store can do this; `unreached`: the Store could not be reached.

asksNothing.description: The plan asks nothing of the apps it offers: an install asked for and nothing else. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

installed.description: With `gap` only, once an app the gap offered with nothing asked of it is installed: the app's id and name, and one of its card's example questions when it has one. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

offered.description: With `source` only, while pending: the offer the region came from, kept until the installed app's first answer — the gap's words, every app the offer offered, and the app installed there. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

Attribution.description: Names the source of a region’s content. A quiet marker that expands to full detail on hover or focus. With a `child`, it is the wrapper of that region: the marker over the content, the two moving as one box of the layout. Painted by the shell around each fragment slot; never authored by a model.

displayName.description: The display name of the app whose content fills the region.

source.description: The source id of the region: the app and the account it painted under.

account.description: The label from the sign-in of the account the content was fetched with; null when the app has a single account.

escalation.description: A scope request inside the region waiting on Allow or Not now. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

scopes.description: The missing scopes only, in the words of the app's card.

child.description: The unique identifier for a component, used for both definitions and references within the same surface.

weight.description: The relative weight of this box within a Row or Column, similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Copied from the wrapped Slot.

fromOffer.description: The wrapped region still shows the offer its app was installed from: the marker waits for the app's first answer. Painted by the runtime and never written by an author.

DerivedValue.description: A value computed across sources on a merged view, shown together with how many sources contributed. Every path of the derived data model whose leaf is a formula renders through this component and no other: bind `cell` to that path (inside a template, relative to the element) and the runtime supplies the value with its contributor state, so a value that is partial, absent, or awaiting recomputation never reads as complete.

cell.description: Path to a formula leaf of the derived data model — e.g. `/counts/gmail`, or `when` inside a row template over `/entries`. The runtime writes the evaluated cell there: the value with its contributor state. Always a path, never a literal.

oneOf.description: Invokes a named function, combining common function properties with the catalog function definition.

format.description: How to render the value. Fixed; not data-bound.

kind.description: text shows the value as is; number groups digits; currency formats a number in the given currency; datetime renders a date-and-time — in whatever form the source painted it — as one readable date and time, the same form for every source.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, required when kind is currency.

prefix.description: Written before the value when there is one — e.g. `#` over a pull request's number, so the cell reads `#8`. The value itself, its sort and its tap stay the source's.

danger.description: The values of this column a reader must act on — e.g. `["Failed"]` on a CI status, in the words the source uses. When the evaluated value is one of them (compared word by word: case and punctuation do not count), the runtime draws it in the danger tone. Fixed; not data-bound; never shown.

SortControl.description: Shows which key an array of the merged view is sorted by and lets the user change the key and the direction. Place one for each sort declaration you emit; bind `sort` to that declaration's runtime state at `/sorts/N`, where N is its index in your `sorts`. The options and their labels are the ones you declared; the runtime keeps the user's choice and re-sorts on change.

sort.description: Path to a sort declaration's runtime state, `/sorts/N`: the sorted array's path, the sortable keys with labels, the current key and direction, as written by the runtime from your declaration. Always a path, never a literal.

oneOf.description: Invokes a named function, combining common function properties with the catalog function definition.

Table.description: A table of like entries: fixed column headings across the top and one row per entry, every column aligned down the table. Use it for a merged list with several values per entry — it is the only shape whose columns line up; a heading Row over a Column of Rows never does. The rows are TableRow components: for a list of the merged view, a template over its array.

columns.description: The column headings, in order, one per cell of each row. Yours to write; fixed, never bound.

columnSources.description: One entry per column, in column order: the source id the column belongs to — the one source whose values it shows — or null for a column of no single source, such as a value computed across sources. The same length as `columns`. Start from the plan's. A column whose source brought no data is drawn reserved from that source's state: its heading says the source is loading or unavailable, and its cells hold a bar or the empty dash in place of yours until the source is included. Fixed, never bound.

children.description: The rows: TableRow ids, or a template over an array of the model whose componentId is a TableRow.

TableRow.description: One row of a Table. Its children are the cells, one per column in the table's column order — a DerivedValue for every value drawn from a source. Only meaningful inside a Table.

DataList.description: The labelled values of one thing — an entry's fields, a summary, a detail — each a label beside its value. Its children are DataListItem components. Not for many like entries side by side; that is a Table.

orientation.description: horizontal puts each label beside its value; vertical stacks the label above it.

children.description: The items: DataListItem ids, or a template over an array of the model whose componentId is a DataListItem.

DataListItem.description: One labelled value inside a DataList: the label is yours to write, the value is its one child — a DerivedValue when it comes from a source.

child.description: The unique identifier for a component, used for both definitions and references within the same surface.

required.description: Checks that the value is not null, undefined, or empty.

regex.description: Checks that the value matches a regular expression string.

pattern.description: The regular expression to search for in the value. Uses the A2UI regex dialect: a portable subset of ECMAScript pattern syntax in Unicode mode with no flags. Matching is case-sensitive, '.' excludes line terminators, and '^' and '$' match only at the ends of the value. Backreferences, lookbehind, named groups and '\p{...}' are not allowed. Patterns longer than 256 code points or that could backtrack catastrophically are rejected.

email.description: Checks that the value is a valid email address.

formatString.description: Performs string interpolation of data model values and other functions in the catalog functions list and returns the resulting string. The value string can contain interpolated expressions in the `${expression}` format. Supported expression types include: JSON Pointer paths to the data model (e.g., `${/absolute/path}` or `${relative/path}`), and renderer-side function calls (e.g., `${now()}`). Function arguments must be named (e.g., `${formatDate(value:${/currentDate}, format:'MM-dd')}`). To include a literal `${` sequence, escape it as `\${`.

formatNumber.description: Formats a number with the specified grouping and decimal precision.

decimals.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to show. Defaults to 0 or 2 depending on locale.

grouping.description: Optional. If true, uses locale-specific grouping separators (e.g. '1,000'). If false, returns raw digits (e.g. '1000'). Defaults to true.

formatCurrency.description: Formats a number as a currency string.

decimals.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to show. Defaults to 0 or 2 depending on locale.

grouping.description: Optional. If true, uses locale-specific grouping separators (e.g. '1,000'). If false, returns raw digits (e.g. '1000'). Defaults to true.

formatDate.description: Formats a timestamp into a string using a pattern.

format.description:
A Unicode TR35 date pattern string.

Token Reference:
- Year: 'yy' (26), 'yyyy' (2026)
- Month: 'M' (1), 'MM' (01), 'MMM' (Jan), 'MMMM' (January)
- Day: 'd' (1), 'dd' (01), 'E' (Tue), 'EEEE' (Tuesday)
- Hour (12h): 'h' (1-12), 'hh' (01-12) - requires 'a' for AM/PM
- Hour (24h): 'H' (0-23), 'HH' (00-23) - Military Time
- Minute: 'mm' (00-59)
- Second: 'ss' (00-59)
- Period: 'a' (AM/PM)

Examples:
- 'MMM dd, yyyy' -> 'Jan 16, 2026'
- 'HH:mm' -> '14:30' (Military)
- 'h:mm a' -> '2:30 PM'
- 'EEEE, d MMMM' -> 'Friday, 16 January'

pluralize.description: Returns a localized string based on the Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR) plural category of the count (zero, one, two, few, many, other). Requires an 'other' fallback. For English, just use 'one' and 'other'.

value.description: The numeric value used to determine the plural category.

two.description: String for the 'two' category (used in Arabic, Welsh, etc.).

few.description: String for the 'few' category (e.g., small groups in Slavic languages).

many.description: String for the 'many' category (e.g., large groups in various languages).

other.description: The default/fallback string (used for general plural cases).

openUrl.description: Opens the specified URL in a browser or handler (requires user activation). This function has no return value.

and.description: Performs a logical AND operation on a list of boolean values.

values.description: The list of boolean values to evaluate.

or.description: Performs a logical OR operation on a list of boolean values.

values.description: The list of boolean values to evaluate.

not.description: Performs a logical NOT operation on a boolean value.

value.description: Passes a single value through unchanged. The operator for a merged-surface cell that shows one source's value as it is.

min.description: The smallest of the given numbers.

max.description: The largest of the given numbers.

sum.description: The sum of the given numbers.

avg.description: The arithmetic mean of the given numbers.

difference.description: The gap between two numbers: the larger less the smaller, never negative. Exactly two numbers; with only one, there is no difference.

argmin.description: The zero-based position of the smallest of the given numbers.

argmax.description: The zero-based position of the largest of the given numbers.

source.description: The source an entry comes from: the app whose partition the first resolving input was read from. Written by the runtime as the app's id — the way to say which source a merged row belongs to without copying a value.

values.description: One or more values; the source of the first that resolves is named.

equal.description: A relation of a match claim, and a fact: the two values are the same. Text compares as its words — letters and digits, case ignored, everything else a break between words; in scripts written without spaces, each character is a word. Two values that each read as a number — a number, or text that is only a number, a currency symbol and grouping separators allowed — compare by value; two date-and-times compare by the moment, to the coarser precision of the two. Two lists of plain values are equal when they have the same members, in any order. An object is never equal to anything. Checked against the data when the synthesis is accepted and live after it: when a value changes, the relation stops holding. Written only inside `match`.

values.description: The two values, each read from a different app.

contains.description: A relation of a match claim, and a fact: the second value is inside the first. Text: the second value's words appear, in order and unbroken, among the first's — words as `equal` reads them, numbers and date-and-times included. A list of plain values: the second value is among its members, compared as `equal` compares them; when the second value is a list too, every member of it is. Checked against the data when the synthesis is accepted and live after it. Written only inside `match`.

values.description: The value that contains, then the value contained, each read from a different app.

judged.description: A relation of a match claim, and your judgment: the two values name the same thing though no fact links them — `equal` and `contains` do not hold, and only understanding joins them. It holds while both values are there and is never checked against what they say. Values tied in only by a judgment are shown as guessed. Written only inside `match`.

values.description: The two values, each read from a different app.

openStore.description: Opens the Store, where apps not yet installed are found and installed. Use from a button when an answer leads the user to look for an app. This function has no return value.

query.description: What to search the Store for, in the user's words. Omit to open the Store without a search.

openAppLibrary.description: Opens the App Library, where installed apps are managed and updated. Use from a button when an answer leads the user to manage or update their apps. This function has no return value.

app.description: The id of one installed app, to open on that app. Omit to open the list of every installed app.

openPublish.description: Opens Publish, where a publisher puts their own app in the Store, sees their apps there and takes one out. Use from a button when an answer leads the user to publish an app. This function has no return value.

Weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
